findings.function: claimCollateral(address[],address[],uint256[],address) and other functions reverting with address-carrying custom errors
findings.issue: Custom-error data is chunked by how it was stored (selector merged with the 12 zero bytes of the next word, then a 20-byte address) instead of as selector + ABI words, so DisabledMarket(address) is unrecognisable; 7 lines here and 1011 lines across the corpus texts have `revert with Bytes(16, 0x...`.
findings.rule: Re-chunk revert (and call) data as a 4-byte selector followed by 32-byte words; a word that is `Bytes(12, 0) ++ x` with x 20 bytes is `address(x)`. Then print `revert with 0x09f8c937, address(_17)` (or the error name).

notes: GMX ExchangeRouter (solc 0.8.29, no via-IR, linked libraries). Most work is delegated to external libraries (FeeUtils.batchClaimFundingFees, ReferralUtils, order/deposit handlers...), so the FeeUtils/ReferralUtils/MarketUtils swap-path/EventUtils loops are not in this bytecode. Source loops in this bytecode: PayableMulticall.multicall (`while idx < data.length`, readable, with ErrorUtils.revertWithParsedMessage inlined correctly) and MarketUtils.batchClaimCollateral (inlined, `while s < _281` in claimCollateral). The other 76 whiles are implicit: calldata array validation, ABI encodes of arrays into library/handler calls, decodes of returned arrays (P7), and the rotated new-bytes[] initialisation in multicall (P3). Immutables (dataStore, handlers, router) read as 0: artifact. The revert string of multicall's Error(string) path and keys such as keccak256(abi.encode("CLAIMABLE_COLLATERAL_AMOUNT")) stay as memory slices because `_x = mem[64]` is not identified with later mem[64] (see c00026). claimCollateral (946 lines) reviewed by structure.
summary: Faithful router text whose two source loops are shown as readable whiles; the noise is implicit ABI copy loops, raw-memory error/key construction, and custom errors printed as unaligned byte chunks.
